{{Joe Biden series|expanded=U.S. senator from Delaware}}
The '''1990 United States Senate election in Delaware''' was held on November 6, 1990. Incumbent Democratic U.S. Senator [[Joe Biden]] won re-election to a fourth term, defeating Republican challenger Deputy [[Attorney General of Delaware]] [[M. Jane Brady]]. Brady decided to run because she felt that Biden's liberal voting record did not reflect the political positions of Delawareans.

Brady's campaign raised around $245,000, but she was heavily outspent by Biden, who raised around $2.8 million. Libertarian candidate Lee Rosenbaum also ran but only received less than two percent of the vote. Debates between the three candidates occurred in late October and early November. Issues for the campaign included fiscal responsibility, the president's [[Veto power in the United States|veto power]], and the role of Congress in the nation's diplomatic relations.

The election had a turnout rate of under 40% of registered voters. Biden won in a landslide with over 60% of the vote, improving on his 1984 margin, winning all three counties and all 41 [[Delaware House of Representatives|State House of Representatives]] districts.

== Background ==
{{Main|1984 United States Senate election in Delaware}}
In 1984, despite [[Ronald Reagan]]'s [[1984 United States presidential election|landslide presidential victory]] in the concurrent election,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Raines |first=Howell |date=November 7, 1984 |title=Reagan Wins By a Landslide, Sweeping at Least 48 States; G.O.P. Gains Strength in House |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1984/11/07/politics/reagan-wins-by-a-landslide-sweeping-at-least-48-states-gop-gains.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825144938/http://www.nytimes.com/1984/11/07/politics/07REAG.html?pagewanted=1 |archive-date=August 25, 2017 |access-date=March 12, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Joe Biden won re-election to a third term, defeating Republican challenger [[John M. Burris]] with a little over 60% of the vote.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ladd |first=Thomas E. |date=May 1, 1985 |title=Statistics of the Presidential and Congressional Election of November 6, 1984 |url=https://clerk.house.gov/member_info/electionInfo/1984election.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210129075653/https://clerk.house.gov/member_info/electionInfo/1984election.pdf |archive-date=January 29, 2021 |access-date=March 11, 2025 |website=[[Clerk of the United States House of Representatives]] |page=10}}</ref><ref name=":2" />

Due to Biden's popularity, Delaware Republicans struggled to find a candidate to challenge him. He was expected to easily win re-election.<ref name=":6" /> The election was held as part of the [[United States midterm election|midterm election cycle]] of Republican President [[George H. W. Bush]]'s term.<ref name=":10" /> Historically, the president's party struggles during the midterms.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Elving |first=Ron |date=November 13, 2022 |title=The midterms didn't produce a wave. Here's what that's meant historically |url=https://www.npr.org/2022/11/13/1136103595/the-midterms-didnt-produce-a-wave-heres-what-thats-meant-historically |access-date=2025-04-01 |work=[[NPR]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Candidates ==
;Nominees
*[[Joe Biden]] ([[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]]), incumbent Delaware senator running for a fourth term{{Sfn|Harper|1991|p=2}}<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Biden, Joseph Robinette (Joe), Jr. (1942–) |url=https://bioguideretro.congress.gov/Home/MemberDetails?memIndex=b000444 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250225204059/https://bioguideretro.congress.gov/Home/MemberDetails?memIndex=b000444 |archive-date=February 25, 2025 |access-date=March 11, 2025 |website=[[Biographical Directory of the United States Congress]]}}</ref>
* [[M. Jane Brady]] ([[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]]), a criminal prosecutor and Deputy Attorney General of Delaware{{Sfn|Harper|1991|p=2}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Honorable M. Jane Brady, Judge |url=https://courts.delaware.gov/superior/aboutus/judges_profile_jbrady.aspx |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211008192514/https://courts.delaware.gov/superior/aboutus/judges_profile_jbrady.aspx |archive-date=October 8, 2021 |access-date=August 1, 2021 |website=[[Delaware Superior Court]]}}</ref>
* Lee Rosenbaum ([[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian]]), a data communications technician{{Sfn|Harper|1991|p=2}}<ref name=":5">{{Cite news |last=Stewart |first=Ann |date=July 22, 1990 |title=Libertarian Party sets ticket of candidates |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/159436052/?match=1&terms=Lee%20Rosenbaum |access-date=March 22, 2025 |website=[[The News Journal]] |page=1 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

;Eliminated in primaries
* David S. DeRiemer (Libertarian)<ref name=":5" />

=== Primaries ===
At the 1990 [[Delaware Democratic Party]] state convention, Biden revealed that he was running for a fourth term, stating that he made the decision to seek re-election during a hospital stay.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cohen |first=Celia |date=March 4, 1990 |title=Democrats eye '92 at annual powwow |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/159556564/?terms=Joe%20Biden |access-date=March 22, 2025 |work=[[The News Journal]] |page=15 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> Biden echoed this statement in an interview with [[C-SPAN]], saying that it was "[n]ot difficult at all. Ironically, it was less difficult than any of the other decisions." He added that he came significantly closer to not running in 1978 and 1984.<ref name=":02" group="‡">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.c-span.org/program/interview/delaware-senate-campaign/151099 |title=Delaware Senate Campaign |date=August 6, 1990 |last=Biden |first=Joe |author-link=Joe Biden |type=Video |publisher=[[C-SPAN]] |time=00:27}}</ref>

The [[Delaware Republican Party]] struggled to find a candidate to challenge Biden. Party chairman Basil Battaglia reached out to the newspaper ''[[The News Journal]]'' to help find candidates.<ref name=":6">{{Cite news |last=Moyed |first=Ralph |date=February 18, 1990 |title=Wanted! (Preferably alive) GOP candidates |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/159554495/?match=1&terms=Joe%20Biden |access-date=March 22, 2025 |work=[[The News Journal]] |page=21 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> The party eventually reached out to Deputy [[Attorney General of Delaware]] [[M. Jane Brady]] due to her history as a criminal prosecutor.<ref name=":12" group="‡">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.c-span.org/program/interview/delaware-senate-campaign/151098 |title=Delaware Senate Campaign |date=August 19, 1990 |last=Brady |first=M. Jane |author-link=M. Jane Brady |type=Video |publisher=[[C-SPAN]] |time=00:36 |access-date=March 12, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250215163441/https://www.c-span.org/program/interview/delaware-senate-campaign/151098 |archive-date=February 15, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> She launched her campaign on May 16, 1990,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Celia |first=Cohen |date=May 17, 1990 |title=Jane Brady challenges Biden for Senate seat |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/159594216/?match=1&terms=Jane%20Brady |access-date=March 18, 2025 |work=[[The News Journal]] |pages=1–2 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> and resigned from her position shortly after.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cohen |first=Celia |date=September 11, 1994 |title=Brady gets GOP blessing |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/157245398/?match=1&terms=Jane%20Brady |access-date=March 22, 2025 |work=[[The News Journal]] |page=1 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> She stated that her decision to run was made after she learned of [[Political positions of Joe Biden|Biden's liberal voting record]] and felt that it "just does not reflect the views of the people of Delaware".<ref name=":12" group="‡" /> Brady identified herself as a conservative, though noting that she held some [[socially liberal]] beliefs.<ref group="‡">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.c-span.org/program/interview/delaware-senate-campaign/151098 |title=Delaware Senate Campaign |date=August 19, 1990 |last=Brady |first=M. Jane |author-link=M. Jane Brady |type=Video |publisher=[[C-SPAN]] |time=02:44}}</ref>

The state convention of the [[Libertarian Party of Delaware]] was held on July 22, 1990. This was the only contested nomination. Lee Rosenbaum, a data communications technician, defeated David S. DeRiemer.<ref name=":5" />

== Issues ==
Biden's early withdrawal from his [[Joe Biden 1988 presidential campaign|1988 presidential campaign]] was considered an issue for the campaign.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.c-span.org/program/interview/delaware-senate-campaign/151098 |title=Delaware Senate Campaign |date=August 19, 1990 |last=Brady |first=M. Jane |author-link=M. Jane Brady |type=Video |publisher=[[C-SPAN]] |time=9:33 |access-date=March 18, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250215163441/https://www.c-span.org/program/interview/delaware-senate-campaign/151098 |archive-date=February 15, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In August 1990, Brady criticized Biden's use of the [[franking privilege]] granted to members of Congress, stating that he could have instead used campaign funds.<ref group="‡">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.c-span.org/program/interview/delaware-senate-campaign/151098 |title=Delaware Senate Campaign |date=August 19, 1990 |last=Brady |first=M. Jane |author-link=M. Jane Brady |type=Video |publisher=[[C-SPAN]] |time=5:24}}</ref> She stated that if elected, she would work to eliminate the privileges.<ref group="‡">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.c-span.org/program/interview/delaware-senate-campaign/151098 |title=Delaware Senate Campaign |date=August 19, 1990 |last=Brady |first=M. Jane |author-link=M. Jane Brady |type=Video |publisher=[[C-SPAN]] |time=15:01 |access-date=March 12, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250215163441/https://www.c-span.org/program/interview/delaware-senate-campaign/151098 |archive-date=February 15, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Throughout the campaign, Brady called for budget reform.<ref group="‡">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.c-span.org/program/interview/delaware-senate-campaign/151098 |title=Delaware Senate Campaign |date=August 19, 1990 |last=Brady |first=M. Jane |author-link=M. Jane Brady |type=Video |publisher=[[C-SPAN]] |time=12:40 |access-date=March 12, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250215163441/https://www.c-span.org/program/interview/delaware-senate-campaign/151098 |archive-date=February 15, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> Brady stated she opposed raising taxes unless it was accompanied by long-term budgetary reform. She suggested a constitutional amendment to limit tax increases.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":8" />

In October 1990, ''[[The News Journal]]'' asked the various candidates what they believed the most pressing issues for the country were. Biden stated that international relations with the then-declining USSR and providing better conditions for children were important in determining the future of the country. Brady stated that her two biggest concerns were fiscal and congressional responsibility, calling for term limits, shorter congressional sessions, and expansion of executive power. Rosenbaum identified the United States's involvement in the [[Gulf War]] as the biggest issue, stating that if elected, he would work to limit the United States's involvement in war. He also advocated for looser drug laws.<ref name=":7">{{Cite news |last=Nagengast |first=Larry |date=October 28, 1990 |title=Voters guide |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/159494323/ |access-date=March 23, 2025 |work=[[The News Journal]] |page=2 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

Biden stated that Congress should focus on improving diplomatic relations with the declining USSR and prioritize [[nuclear disarmament]], while Brady felt that Congress should avoid dealing with foreign relations and instead delegate the job to the [[Department of Defense]].<ref name=":8" />

== Election ==

=== Campaign ===
Speaking with C-SPAN, Biden stated he planned to campaign similarly to how he did in his previous elections,<ref group="‡">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.c-span.org/program/interview/delaware-senate-campaign/151099 |title=Delaware Senate Campaign |date=August 6, 1990 |last=Biden |first=Joe |author-link=Joe Biden |type=Video |publisher=[[C-SPAN]] |time=03:08}}</ref> although he noted that he would have less time to campaign due to his role in overseeing [[David Souter]]'s nomination to the [[Supreme Court of the United States|Supreme Court]] due to his role on the [[Senate Judiciary Committee]].<ref group="‡">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.c-span.org/program/interview/delaware-senate-campaign/151099 |title=Delaware Senate Campaign |date=August 6, 1990 |last=Biden |first=Joe |author-link=Joe Biden |type=Video |publisher=[[C-SPAN]] |time=04:10}}</ref> Biden had previously used his position on the committee to reject [[Robert Bork Supreme Court nomination|Ronald Reagan's nomination]] of [[Robert Bork]] to the Supreme Court. Brady criticized this, stating his role in the Bork hearings was evidence of Biden's poor character.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=October 14, 1990 |title=Senate campaigns resort to video |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/948384349/?match=1&terms=Jane%20Brady |access-date=March 18, 2025 |work=[[United Press International]] |publisher=[[Troy Daily News]] |page=7 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

''[[The News Journal]]'' wrote that they felt voters in Delaware knew little about Brady. Brady noted that she frequently sent them press releases, and cases she worked on often received news coverage.<ref group="‡">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.c-span.org/program/interview/delaware-senate-campaign/151098 |title=Delaware Senate Campaign |date=August 19, 1990 |last=Brady |first=M. Jane |author-link=M. Jane Brady |type=Video |publisher=[[C-SPAN]] |time=02:02 |access-date=March 12, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250215163441/https://www.c-span.org/program/interview/delaware-senate-campaign/151098 |archive-date=February 15, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Despite Brady being one of few women running for Senate in 1990, Biden was endorsed by various prominent women in the [[Government of Delaware]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 2, 1990 |title=Women leaders back Biden's re-election bid |work=[[The News Journal]] |page= |pages=10–11 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Dole |first=Bob |author-link=Bob Dole |date=June 9, 1992 |title=GOP's Women candidates get no respect or publicity |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |publisher=[[Albuquerque Journal]] |page=7 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> Additionally, due to a childcare bill he co-sponsored, Biden received the endorsements of several childcare activists.<ref name=":9" />

On October 2, 1990, she accused Biden of hiring staff from his [[Joe Biden 1988 presidential campaign|presidential campaign]] to work for him in the Senate, labeling it as an "abuse of public trust and a misuse of public funds". [[Ted Kaufman]], Biden's then-chief of staff, stated that this was not unusual for a Senate Committee chairman.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kesler |first=Nancy |date=October 2, 1990 |title=Brady Accuses Biden of Juggling Staff in '87 |work=[[The News Journal]] |page=10}}</ref>

A televised debate between Biden, Brady, and Rosenbaum was held on October 23 by First State News and Heritage Cablevision.<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 23, 1990 |title=Television Today |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/159488749/?match=1&terms=Lee%20Rosenbaum%20libertarian |access-date=March 23, 2025 |work=[[The News Journal]] |page=32 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=October 23, 1990 |title=Vote your choice! |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/159488820/ |work=[[The News Journal]] |page=36 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> A radio debate between them was held on November 2 on [[WILM (AM)|WILM]]. In the debate Biden and Brady argued over [[line-item veto]]s. Brady felt that the president should be able to veto specific parts of bills, while Biden felt that it would give the president too much power, allowing them to "take complete control" of Congress.<ref name=":9">{{Cite news |last=Kesler |first=Nancy |date=November 3, 1990 |title=Biden, Brady air differences on veto |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/159466833/ |access-date=March 30, 2025 |work=[[The News Journal]] |page=2 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

Brady stated that she hoped to win the election without accepting donations from [[Special interest groups in the United States|special interest groups]].<ref group="‡">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.c-span.org/program/interview/delaware-senate-campaign/151098 |title=Delaware Senate Campaign |date=August 19, 1990 |last=Brady |first=M. Jane |author-link=M. Jane Brady |type=Video |publisher=[[C-SPAN]] |time=8:22 |access-date=March 12, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250215163441/https://www.c-span.org/program/interview/delaware-senate-campaign/151098 |archive-date=February 15, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> Ultimately, both Brady and Biden accepted money from interest groups.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Moyed |first=Ralph |date=November 4, 1990 |title=Reform politics? Why take all the fun out of the game |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/159471596/ |access-date=March 31, 2025 |work=[[The News Journal]] |page=3 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> Brady's campaign raised around $200,000 by October 14 and around $245,000 by election day.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4" /> She decided against running television commercials and for mailing videotapes instead, as it would be cheaper. The videotapes heavily attacked Biden, leading to them generating controversy.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":8">{{Cite news |last=Kesler |first=Nancy |date=October 28, 1990 |title=Rivels Brady, Biden spar from afar |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/159493032/ |access-date=March 23, 2025 |work=[[The News Journal]] |pages=2, 14 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> The campaign spent most of its funds, having $4,117 left over after the election.<ref name=":4" /> She was heavily outspent by Biden, who raised around 2.8 million dollars, spending around 2.6 million. He ended his campaign with $190,151 left.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=1990 Election United States Senate – Delaware |url=https://www.fec.gov/data/elections/senate/DE/1990/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170820163144/https://www.fec.gov/data/elections/senate/DE/1990/ |archive-date=August 20, 2017 |access-date=March 12, 2025 |website=[[Federal Election Commission]] |language=en}}</ref>

=== Results ===
Polls closed at 8 p.m.,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rove |first=Karl |date=2021-03-31 |title=Opinion {{!}} Biden's Election-Reform Deception |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/bidens-election-reform-deception-11617229306 |access-date=2025-03-23 |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660}}</ref> and the [[Associated Press]] called the race for Biden at 8:42 p.m.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mullinax |first=Gary |date=November 7, 1990 |title=Reporting of results from Delaware spotty on the tube |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/159477243/?match=1&terms=Joe%20Biden |access-date=March 22, 2025 |work=[[The News Journal]] |page=15 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> Around 10:30 p.m., Brady conceded; she partially blamed President [[George H. W. Bush]]'s role in the passing of the [[Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1990|Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act]].<ref name=":11">{{Cite news |last=Kesler |first=Nancy |date=November 7, 1990 |title=Biden buried Brady in Senate |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/159477189/ |access-date=April 1, 2025 |work=[[The News Journal]] |pages=13 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> Biden, like most incumbents in the [[1990 United States Senate elections]], was reelected to another term.<ref name=":10">{{Cite news |last1=Dewar |first1=Helen |last2=Yang |first2=John E. |date=November 6, 1990 |title=The Senate Incumbents Win Control Remains with Democrats |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/1990/11/07/the-senate/88a317b4-abae-4a7c-9a3c-f65fe6b52b54/ |access-date=March 12, 2025 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}}</ref> He won in a landslide, receiving 62.68% of the vote.<ref name=":11" /><ref name=":03">{{Cite web |last=Leip |first=David |title=1990 Senatorial General Election Results - Delaware |url=https://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/state.php?year=1990&fips=10&f=0&off=3&elect=0&class=2 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150912111215/http://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/state.php?fips=10&year=1990&f=0&off=3&elect=0&class=2 |archive-date=2015-09-12 |access-date=2025-03-11 |website=[[Dave Leip's Atlas of U.S. Presidential Elections]]}}</ref> A slight improvement on his previous margin of victory.{{Sfn|Dennis|1985|p=2}} Five votes were cast for write-in candidates.<ref name=":03" /> The election had a turnout rate of under 40%—slightly higher than that of the concurrent [[1990 United States House of Representatives election in Delaware|House of Representatives election]] for [[Delaware's at-large congressional district]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last=Dendy |first=Dallas L. |url=https://clerk.house.gov/member_info/electionInfo/1990election.pdf |title=Statistics of the Congressional Election of November 6, 1990 |date=April 29, 1991 |publisher=[[Clerk of the United States House of Representatives]] |page=8 |access-date=March 12, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210110062943/https://clerk.house.gov/member_info/electionInfo/1990election.pdf |archive-date=January 10, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Both Biden and Rosenbaum performed worse than their Democrat and Libertarian counterparts in the election for the House district. However, Brady outperformed Republican nominee Ralph O'Williams by three percent.<ref name=":1" /> With the exception of [[Tom Carper]] in the House race, Biden outperformed all other Democratic, Republican, and Libertarian nominees for all of Delaware's [[at-large]] elections, including Attorney General, State Treasurer, and [[Delaware Auditor of Accounts|Auditor of Accounts]]. With the exception of O'Williams, Brady underperformed the Republican nominees for all other at-large elections. Rosenbaum was the worst-performing Libertarian nominee.{{Sfn|Harper|1991|p=2}}

==== By subdivision ====
Biden won all three counties for the third election in a row.{{Sfn|Wrightson|1978|p=2}}{{Sfn|Dennis|1985|p=8}} Biden's best performance was in [[New Castle County, Delaware|New Castle County]], where he won 62 percent of the vote to Brady's 36 percent. Brady's best performance was in [[Kent County, Delaware|Kent County]], where she won around 40 percent of the vote to Biden's 58 percent, his lowest share of the vote. Kent County was also Rosenbaum's best performance, where he won slightly under two percent. New Castle County had the highest number of votes cast, with 103 thousand, followed by [[Sussex County, Delaware|Sussex County]] with 86 thousand.{{Sfn|Harper|1991|p=2}}

Biden won all 41 representative districts; in the concurrent legislative election, 24 Republican candidates won seats.{{Sfn|Harper|1991|pp=8, 12}} He won all of them by a [[majority]] of the vote. Biden's best performance was in District 20, where he received 4,260 votes. Rosenbaum also saw his highest vote total in the district with 106 votes. District 20 was additionally the district where the highest number of votes were cast. Biden's worst performance came in District 34, where he received 1,593 votes to Brady's 1,377. Brady saw her best performance in District 11 with 2,999 votes to Biden's 3,111.{{Sfn|Harper|1991|p=12}}

== Aftermath ==
On January 3, 1991, Biden was sworn in to the [[102nd United States Congress]] by then–Vice President [[Dan Quayle]] alongside his fellow Senator-elects.<ref>{{Cite video |url=https://www.c-span.org/program/senate-highlight/swearing-in-of-senate-members/10810 |title=Swearing-In of Senate Members |date=January 3, 1991 |type=Video |publisher=[[C-SPAN]] |time=5:27}}</ref> During the following [[1992 United States elections|election cycle]], [[Senate minority leader]] [[Bob Dole]] criticized the lack of media coverage that Brady, along with other female Republican candidates, received.<ref name=":32">{{Cite news |last=Dole |first=Bob |author-link=Bob Dole |date=June 9, 1992 |title=GOP's Women Candidates Get No Respect or Publicity |department=Opinion |agency=''[[The Washington Post]]'' |newspaper=[[Albuquerque Journal]] |page=7}}</ref> During the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 presidential election]], Brady spoke about Biden, stating, "I don't think he ever broke a sweat once he was an incumbent".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Epstein |first=Reid J. |date=2024-05-02 |title=Joe Biden, the Ultimate D.C. Veteran, Has Never Seen a Campaign Like This |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/05/02/us/politics/biden-election-campaign-opponents.html |access-date=2025-03-31 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>
